candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; identify barriers to care, coordinate referrals/resources, support continuity, and advocate for access to prescribed treatment
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — financial barriers and equitable access to diabetes technology
candidate.educational_objective: Identify and address financial or insurance barriers to diabetes technology early by coordinating coverage and support resources to reduce avoidable interruption of effective therapy.

options.A: Assess the financial and insurance barrier, notify the diabetes care team, and connect the client with appropriate coverage, social-service, or lower-cost support resources before access is interrupted.
options.B: Assume technology access depends only on personal preference and continue the plan without addressing cost or coverage.
options.C: Tell the client to stop using diabetes technology permanently because financial barriers cannot be modified by the care team.
options.D: Wait until the client has already run out of sensors before discussing access because insurance status is not relevant to treatment planning.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care direct clinicians to assess financial barriers, health insurance, and health care access as social determinants that can affect diabetes management and to collaborate with the care team and social-service resources to reduce cost-related barriers. ADA also recognizes geographic and socioeconomic variation in diabetes-technology adoption and emphasizes continued access to devices and supplies. B, C, and D fail to address a modifiable barrier that can disrupt evidence-based care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Financial, insurance, socioeconomic, and access barriers can affect diabetes care and technology use; current ADA guidance requires assessment of such barriers and collaborative efforts to preserve access to evidence-based treatment and supplies.
candidate.source_document_title: Improving Care and Promoting Health in Populations: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; Diabetes Technology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: Section 1 Recommendations 1.6–1.7 — assess insurance status, financial barriers, health insurance and health care access and refer to resources; Section 9 Recommendation 9.29 — routinely assess financial obstacles and collaborate to reduce costs; Section 7 — geographic and socioeconomic variation in pump/AID adoption and need for continued technology access
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: A client using continuous glucose monitoring says, “My insurance changed and I may not be able to afford the sensors next month.” Which nursing action best supports equitable diabetes care?
